html:
On 22 May 2015 Irish voters approved same-sex marriage in a referendum, by 62 percent. Ireland was the first country to do so by popular vote.

Homosexual acts had been a crime in Ireland until 1993. The Catholic Church had long shaped Irish law, as in the constitution written by de Valera in 1937, but its authority fell after reports from the 1990s on child abuse by clergy. Young emigrants flew home to vote.

In 2018 a further referendum removed the near-total ban on abortion. The two votes showed how far Ireland had changed since the Celtic Tiger years. Compare the Netherlands, the first country to allow same-sex marriage, in 2001.
sum: On 22 May 2015 Irish voters approved same-sex marriage in a referendum, by 62 percent. Ireland was the first country to do so by popular vote.
